country: United States (Boston Children's Hospital); external US and international centers

links.outcome: Critical CHD detection AUROC internal test versus external referral cohort
links.effect: Internal AUROC 0.94 for composite critical CHD fell to 0.77 on the referral cohort, showing internal validation overstated performance at external sites.
links.quote: Performance declined during evaluation on the referral cohort to detect critical CHD (AUROC, 0.77), coinciding with greater expert disagreement on referral cases (κ=0.72 versus 0.82 for internal cases).

links.outcome: Performance drop at new sites; domain shift between cohorts
links.effect: Critical CHD AUROC dropped from 0.94 internal to 0.77 in the referral cohort; UMAP analysis revealed domain shift between cohorts.
links.quote: whereas uniform manifold approximation and projection analysis revealed a domain shift between cohorts.

links.outcome: International critical CHD AUROC and calibration after retraining on all available US patients
links.effect: Retraining on all available US patients attenuated domain shift, improving international critical CHD AUROC to 0.87 and improving calibration.
links.quote: Retraining on all available US patients attenuated domain shift effects, improving international critical CHD detection (AUROC, 0.87) and calibration.

unlisted_practices: Explainability analysis showing the model attends to clinically relevant echo views across cohorts

screen.reason: The study tests an echocardiography diagnostic deep learning model across internal and external cohorts, directly testing and evaluating domain shift mitigation via retraining on diverse cohorts before deployment.
